artifacts.summary: Confirms both compounding causes (genuinely-external source store in a consumer repository; an unexpanded $SD token authored directly in plan prose and harvested verbatim), identifies V9's existing out-of-repository classification in git-commit-scoped.sh as directly reusable precedent, maps the open-backlog boundary against tasks 508/517/548, and recommends a sanctioned source-store marker plus a Site-2 out-of-repository pre-check and second-repository commit step.

memory_candidates.content: git-commit-scoped.sh's V9 gate already classifies a pathspec resolving outside the repository root as a distinct case (its own out_of_repo_dropped ledger, exit code, and textually-distinct WARN), separate from V10's file_scope containment drop. When investigating a 'not contained in declared file_scope' drop for a path that might actually be outside the repository entirely, check whether the drop happened upstream (e.g. git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check) before V9 ever got a chance to classify it correctly -- the upstream site's generic message can mask a genuinely different root cause.

.claude-extensions.json's source_dir is resolved per-extension (jq -r '.extensions.<name>.source_dir'); a top-level jq -r '.source_dir' returns null and must never be read as the key being absent. Whether a given extension's source_dir is 'external' depends entirely on which repository you resolve it from: the same absolute path can sit inside one repository's own git root (the canonical source-store repository itself) while sitting genuinely outside a different consumer repository's root. Any fix or test for source-store containment must be validated against a genuinely-disjoint consumer-repo scenario, not just the canonical source-store repository's own tree.
